history.dynasty: Mushika (Kolathiri) dynasty; consecration legend attributed to Parashurama
history.period: Legends date it to Treta Yuga; rebuilt into present form in the early 11th century (verify)
history.summary: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala consecrated by Parashurama (legend), a Dwadasha Shivalayam, and one of the ancient Shakti Peethas — legend says the head of Goddess Sati fell here after the Daksha yagna. The swayambhu Shiva lingam (~3 ft, gold-covered) is linked to kings Mandhata, Muchukunda and Satasoma and to sages Agastya and Parashurama; Sri Rama is believed to have worshipped here on his return from Lanka, so the namaskara mandapam is off-limits for prostrations. Renovated by the Mushika/Kolathiri kings and rebuilt in the early 11th century; partially damaged during Tipu Sultan's invasion (verify). Unique customs: no kodimaram (flagstaff), tulsi (not bilva) offered to the lingam, Shiva worshipped on Wednesdays rather than Mondays, women permitted only after the Athazha Pooja (~7:15-8:30 PM) when Shiva is believed to sit with Parvati, and no pradosha celebrations. Administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board.

name: Rajarajeshwara Temple
town_description: Taliparamba (Thaliparamba) is a town in Kannur district, North Kerala, about 25 km north of Kannur city, in the ancient region of Perinchellur (Perumchelloor). It is a major religious centre of North Malabar, forming a trinity of revered temples with the Vaidyanatha temple at Kanhirangat and the Krishna temple at Trichambaram. Well connected by road and rail (Pazhayangadi station ~15 km), with Kannur International Airport the nearest airport.

travel.airport: Kannur International Airport — ~60 km (verify); Calicut International Airport ~139 km
travel.road: Frequent buses from Kannur to Taliparamba; autos from Taliparamba bus stand (~50 INR, verify) to the temple

visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:45 AM-12:00 PM and 4:45 PM-8:30 PM (DTPC Kannur) — verify; women allowed inside the sanctum only after the Athazha Pooja (~7:15-8:30 PM); non-Hindus and mobile phones/electronics are strictly prohibited
